Ramygala Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžys County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Ramygala as early as the end of the 16th century, around the time the town gained the right to hold three annual fairs in 1580; the population peaked at 650 people (49 percent) in the second half of the 19th century. A seven-member Jewish committee oversaw community life once Lithuania granted Jewish autonomy, and though a Yiddish-language school was briefly established, it closed as most local Jews aligned with the Zionist camp, favoring the Hebrew-language Tarbut network instead. A new library, replacing 600 books lost to fire, opened in 1929; a Beit Midrash inaugurated in January 1933, on the ruins of an earlier synagogue destroyed by fire, still stands today marked by a plaque. The entire Jewish community of Ramygala was murdered in the Pajuoste forest on August 24–25, 1941. This cemetery, likely established alongside the town's earliest Jewish settlers at the end of the 16th century, was abandoned during the Soviet era; in 2013, fragments of gravestones found during town construction work were returned to the site.
